sentence: This project runs a central laboratory and biorepository that tracks samples over time to help explain aging and its effects on hemostasis and thrombosis.
This project studies how proteases and their adaptors work together to break down specific proteins in mitochondria.
This project studies how organelles communicate as stem cells become neurons or muscle cells, and how lipid storage organelles connect with other organelles.
This project studies how a sex-specific protein modification changes brain and behavior after heroin use.
This project identifies proteins that let planarians activate and detoxify organophosphorus pesticides to help study how these pesticides cause neurotoxicity.
This project builds mathematical models of how acute myeloid leukemia changes state to predict how individual patients respond to therapy.
This project builds computational methods to study evolution during drug response, especially extrachromosomal DNA and transcriptional programs.
This project studies how inflammatory signals help blood clones with a gene mutation grow, in a condition called clonal hematopoiesis.
This project studies how an immune checkpoint on T cells suppresses immune responses in tumors and affects myeloid cells.
This project builds a marker and a stimulation method that use dynamical systems modeling to find the brain region where seizures start in epilepsy patients.
This project studies which genes limit how long engineered T cells survive in solid tumors.
This project studies how metabolic stress causes injury and cell death in proximal tubular cells through a redox-sensitive corepressor.
This project builds computational methods that combine single-cell datasets from many patient cohorts to find biomarkers.
This project studies how products of bacteria in the small intestine cause abdominal pain in irritable bowel syndrome.
This project uses postmortem imaging of human brains to study how cardiovascular disease and molecular abnormalities damage neurons in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds an automated technology that copies features of the human gut ecosystem to study how antibiotic resistance evolves in bacteria.
This project studies how glioblastoma escapes the immune system after brain cancer vaccines and tests combining vaccination with immune checkpoint inhibition.
This project studies how acid-sensing ion channels control communication between neurons and glioblastoma and how it helps cancer develop.
This project studies how the body controls temperature during heat stress.
This project builds an extended reality platform with AI, soft robotic heart models and fluoroscopy-compatible systems to train clinicians for structural heart procedures.
